{"relevant": true, "severity": "critical", "message": "internal/auth/reset.go: token = md5(email + timestamp) is predictable. An attacker who knows a victim's email can brute-force the timestamp (a few thousand guesses) and take over the account via POST /reset. Fix: generate the token with crypto/rand (32 bytes, base64url-encoded), store only its SHA-256 hash server-side with a short expiry (~15-30 min), make it single-use, and compare with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. Also: return the same response whether or not the email exists (avoids account enumeration), rate-limit /reset per IP and per account, and invalidate existing sessions after the password changes.", "remember": [{"op":"add","scope":"project","kind":"convention","text":"Security-sensitive tokens (reset, session, API) must come from crypto/rand and be stored hashed with an expiry, never derived from md5 or guessable inputs.","paths":["internal/auth/**"]}]}
